identity.title: Entrepreneurship in Healthcare
identity.subtitle: From a Health Need to a Sustainable Venture
identity.credit_policy: The book is credited to Assoc. Prof. Mohamed Yasser Hamdy alone, as the user asked. The revision notes are not credited; the rework writes new text on their topics rather than reproducing their wording. Chanda and Gupta (2025), Healthcare Entrepreneurship and Management (Routledge), which the user supplied as a preview, is used only as a cited reference for structure and ideas; none of its text, figures or data tables is reproduced.
identity.rework_authorised_note: The user commissioned this book from a set of revision notes on entrepreneurship (three lectures with question banks); no written authorisation from their author is on file. The Routledge preview is a copyrighted reference, not a source to be reworked.

domain.primary: Entrepreneurship and venture creation in the health sector
subfields: the entrepreneur: definitions, characteristics, types and stages
why entrepreneurship matters, entrepreneurship development programmes and their problems
the health startup ecosystem in Egypt and worldwide
the task and general environment of a health organisation; outsourcing; barriers to entry
national culture (Hofstede), globalisation and diverse health teams
unmet health needs and need statements
idea generation, empathy maps and personas
customer discovery: patient surveys and competitor analysis
design thinking, minimum viable product and prototyping of health products and services
business models, the Business Model Canvas and the business plan
start-up costs, break-even and funding (bootstrapping, grants, angels, venture capital)
regulation, licensing, quality standards and ethics for health ventures in Egypt
intellectual property and branding of a health venture
launching, growing and failing; social entrepreneurship in health

figures.notes: Diagrams (entrepreneurial stages, task and general environment, Hofstede profile, need-statement funnel, empathy map, design-thinking loop, Business Model Canvas, break-even chart, funding stages, launch roadmap) are drawn as SVG sources in rework/figures.

audience.prior_knowledge: No prior business or economics; basic arithmetic and percentages. Students know their own clinical service (laboratory or imaging) from the practitioner's side.
audience.display_line: For third-year students of the Faculty of Applied Health Sciences

goal.notes: Turn the point-form revision notes into an explained textbook on entrepreneurship in the health sector. The three lectures (entrepreneurship; global organisations; national culture) are kept and applied to health ventures. The book is broadened with the venture-creation path (need, idea, customer, design, MVP, business model, finance, regulation, IP, launch), using Chanda and Gupta (2025) as a cited reference. The foreign cases (Apple, Alibaba, Tesla) are kept briefly, and each chapter adds verified examples of Egyptian health entrepreneurs: laboratory and imaging chains, digital health startups, pharmaceutical companies and social enterprises.

language.terminology: Standard entrepreneurship and business terms (MVP, Business Model Canvas, value proposition, break-even, bootstrapping, angel investor, venture capital, equity, valuation, intellectual property), each defined on first use.

size.restructuring_note: About 14 chapters: the three source lectures open the book in their order (split where a topic needs its own chapter), followed by the venture-creation chapters.

mcq.format: Ten four-option MCQs per chapter tagged to a learning objective, with rationales at the end of the chapter, followed by short essay questions with model answer points. The source question banks are reused where correct and rewritten where weak.

curriculum_standards: NARS (National Academic Reference Standards) for Applied Health Sciences, NAQAAE. No copy is on file, so the book claims no NARS alignment until one is supplied and the objectives are mapped to it
frameworks: Egyptian Personal Data Protection Law No. 151 of 2020
Egyptian intellectual property law (Law No. 82 of 2002)

references.style_note: APA 7 author-date citations in the text; each chapter lists what it cites, and one consolidated reference list closes the book. At least 60% of sources date from 2016 or later; classic sources (Schumpeter, Hofstede, Osterwalder) are kept where they are the origin of a concept. Facts about named Egyptian entrepreneurs and companies cite a public source (company page, reputable press or investor report) with its year.

must_keep: Every topic of the three source lectures, in the source order
The source question banks' correct items, reused or rewritten
must_not_change: No invented ISBN, publisher or copyright registration
No promotional claims for named commercial products or companies

No invented fact about a named person or company: every figure, date and funding amount in an Egyptian example is checked against a cited public source and dated; anything that cannot be checked is left out
No text, figure or data table reproduced from Chanda and Gupta (2025)
